cap_note: User-imposed hard cap of 2 test cases for this run (ING-10 has 10 ACs and 7 delta FRs). The 2 cases below were chosen to (a) exercise the core identity+roster upsert mechanism end-to-end and (b) cover the two HIGH-severity risks from docs/research/ING-10.md (PII-logging, R-1; two-tier validation semantics, R-2). Every AC/FR/NFR left without coverage is listed explicitly in coverage_audit.uncovered — this is a deliberate scope cut, not a derivation gap, and must be escalated before the Product Gate per the run instructions.

test_cases.title: Valid manifest ingest upserts identity, expands aliases, maps roles, returns per-email response
test_cases.given: a valid ingest token scoped to the program and a well-formed manifest payload with an identity block and a team member carrying 2 aliases
test_cases.then: program_summary is upserted from program:, program_roster gains one row per primary email plus each alias with role mapped through role_map, and the response reports per-section received/valid/rejected counts plus per-email created/updated/skipped detail
test_cases.objective: Verify the endpoint's core mechanism: identity upsert, per-alias roster row expansion, role-slug mapping into user_roles, and the contract response shape, in a single well-formed request.
preconditions: A valid ingest token exists whose allowed_program_ids includes program PROG-100
program_summary and program_roster have no pre-existing rows for PROG-100
Alembic migrations applied so program_roster (table #19) exists
steps: Send POST /api/ingest/manifest with the payload above and the valid bearer token scoped to PROG-100
Query program_roster WHERE program_id = 'PROG-100' AND removed_at IS NULL
Query user_roles for alice@example.com and priya@example.com
Inspect the response body's identity and roster count sections and per-email breakdown
expected_results: program_summary.name/type/description for PROG-100 equal 'Order Platform'/'Greenfield'/'Order management modernization'
program_roster holds exactly 3 rows for Alice (alice@example.com, alice.rossi@example.com, a.rossi@example.com), each sharing name='Alice Rossi' and role='dev', each unique on (program_id, email)
program_roster holds exactly 1 row for priya@example.com with role='arch'
user_roles has email='alice@example.com' mapped to role 'developer' (source='file') and email='priya@example.com' mapped to role 'architect' (source='file')
Response body reports identity.received=1/valid=1/rejected=0 and roster.received=2/valid=2/rejected=0, with per-email created=true for both alice@example.com and priya@example.com

test_cases.title: Two-tier validation: bad program.type aborts the whole request; a bad team[] role rejects only that row; no PII is ever logged
test_cases.given: one manifest whose program: block has an out-of-enum type, and a second, separate manifest whose program: block is valid but whose team[] has one entry with an unmapped role slug alongside a valid entry
test_cases.when: POST /api/ingest/manifest processes each request in turn
test_cases.then: the first request is rejected wholesale with 400 and zero writes; the second commits identity and the valid team entry while rejecting only the bad-slug entry with a reason; and every ingest_manifest_write log record emitted for either request contains only the allowlisted fields and never email or name
test_cases.objective: Verify the two-tier validation split (request-level abort vs. row-level rejection, PRD Research Condition C-1) and confirm the PII-logging constraint (Research Condition C-2) holds even while processing payloads that carry real email/name values and even on the rejection paths.
preconditions: A valid ingest token exists whose allowed_program_ids includes program PROG-200
program_summary and program_roster have no pre-existing rows for PROG-200
A log capture fixture is attached to the test process to record the full emitted structured log record (message text + extra dict) for the ingest_manifest_write event
steps: Send Request A (program.type = 'NotARealType') to POST /api/ingest/manifest with the valid bearer token
Assert Request A's response status and query program_summary/program_roster/user_roles for PROG-200 to confirm zero writes
Send Request B (valid program.type, one team entry with role='not_a_real_role') to POST /api/ingest/manifest with the same bearer token
Assert Request B's response status, response body counts, and the resulting program_summary/program_roster/user_roles state
Inspect every captured ingest_manifest_write log record (message + extra dict) emitted during both requests
expected_results: Request A returns 400, and program_summary, program_roster, and user_roles remain completely unwritten for PROG-200 (request-level abort, zero writes)
Request B returns 200; program_summary for PROG-200 is upserted from the valid program: block
Request B's valid entry (sam@example.com, role='pm') commits to program_roster and user_roles (mapped to 'product-manager')
Request B's invalid entry (jo@example.com, role='not_a_real_role') is placed in the roster rejected bucket with a reason, and no row for jo@example.com is written to program_roster or user_roles
Request B's response body reports roster.received=2/valid=1/rejected=1, with the rejection reason attached to jo@example.com

Every captured ingest_manifest_write log record for both requests contains only the fields {program_id, token_label, identity_written, roster_received, roster_valid, roster_created, roster_updated, roster_removed, roster_rejected, duration_ms} and never contains 'email', 'name', 'sam@example.com', 'jo@example.com', 'Sam Lee', or 'Jo Park' — in the structured fields or in the message string
